title: Aspire: Can Models Self-Evolve from Vague Goals?
abstract: arXiv:2608.31111v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Many important forms of human learning begin with a vague goal, such as "become a better physicist" or "improve at research." Learners must interpret the goal, identify capability gaps, decide how to learn, and determine whether they have actually improved. In contrast, existing work on LLM self-evolution typically begins with tasks and evaluation metrics specified by humans, reducing self-evolution to optimizing an explicit objective rather than deciding what and how to learn. We introduce ASPIRE, a benchmark for vague-goal-driven self-evolution. ASPIRE provides only a natural-language capability goal while downstream evaluation tasks remain hidden. The agent must operationalize the goal by choosing data and update methods, constructing training and validation signals, and deciding when to evaluate. translated_title: Aspire：模型能否从模糊目标中实现自我进化？
translated_abstract: 人类学习的许多重要形式都始于一个模糊的目标，例如“成为更好的物理学家”或“提升研究能力”。学习者必须解读目标、识别能力差距、决定如何学习，并判断自己是否真正取得了进步。相比之下，现有关于大语言模型自我进化的研究通常从人类预先指定的任务和评估指标出发，将自我进化简化为对一个显式目标的优化，而非自主决定学什么以及如何学。我们提出了ASPIRE，一个由模糊目标驱动的自我进化基准。ASPIRE仅提供一个自然语言形式的能力目标，而下游评估任务保持隐藏。智能体必须将该目标具体化，包括选择数据和更新方法、构建训练与验证信号，以及决定何时进行评估。ASPIRE在统一的交互式环境中同时支持模型权重层面的进化和智能体框架层面的进化，并对所产生的系统进行评估。
tldr: ASPIRE是一个由模糊自然语言目标驱动的大语言模型自我进化基准，要求智能体在下游评估任务隐藏的情况下，自主将目标具体化为数据选择、训练信号构建和评估时机决策，从而考察模型能否自主决定“学什么”和“如何学”。
en_tdlr: ASPIRE is a benchmark for vague-goal-driven self-evolution of LLMs, where agents must autonomously operationalize a natural-language capability goal—choosing data, update methods, and evaluation timing—while downstream evaluation tasks remain hidden, testing whether models can decide what and how to learn.
